content: 1. Monitor serum potassium levels closely when adjusting the dose of finerenone, as its levels or effects may be increased by ethinylestradiol due to inhibition of hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 2. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for increased adverse effects of flibanserin, especially when co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 3. Drospirenone and flurbiprofen both elevate serum potassium levels. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 4. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 5. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 6. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while formoterol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 7. Fosinopril and drospirenone may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia due to pharmacodynamic interactions. Use caution and monitor potassium levels. 8. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration if possible, or adjust the dose of BCRP substrates. Do not exceed an ethinylestradiol dose of 30 mcg/day. 9. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while furosemide decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 10. Gemifloxacin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while gentamicin decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 12. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 13. Ethinylestradiol increases green tea levels by reducing its elimination. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 14. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may further reduce hemin efficacy. 15. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of hyaluronidase. Estrogens in high systemic doses may render tissues partially resistant to hyaluronidase, requiring larger amounts for equivalent dispersing effects. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while hydrochlorothiazide decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 17. Drospirenone and ibuprofen both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 18. Drospirenone and ibuprofen IV both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 19. Iloperidone increases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 20. Iloperidone, a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor therapy. 21. Imidapril and drospirenone may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia due to pharmacodynamic interactions. Use caution and monitor potassium levels. 22. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while indapamide decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 23. Drospirenone and indomethacin both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 24. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 25. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 26. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of insulin detemir through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 27. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 28. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of insulin glulisine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 29. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 30. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of insulin lispro through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 31. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of insulin NPH through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 32. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of regular human insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 33. Irbesartan and drospirenone both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 34. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 35. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while isoproterenol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 36. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 37. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 38. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. CYP3A4 inhibitors like itraconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. 39. Juniper may potentiate or interfere with diuretic therapy. It has diuretic effects but may cause kidney damage at high doses. Use caution and monitor therapy. 40. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. 41. Drospirenone and ketoprofen both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 42. Drospirenone and ketorolac both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 43. Drospirenone and ketorolac intranasal both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 44. Labetalol and drospirenone both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 45. Drospirenone decreases the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 46. Ethinylestradiol decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Use caution and monitor therapy. 47. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. 48. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while levalbuterol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 49. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lower nightly doses of lemborexant are recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 50. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last SC dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 51. Levofloxacin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 52. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential interactions. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. 53. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 54. Drospirenone reduces the effects of liraglutide by altering passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 55. Lisinopril and drospirenone may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia due to pharmacodynamic interactions. Use caution and monitor potassium levels. 56. Lixisenatide may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by delaying gastric emptying and inhibiting GI absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. Monitor therapy closely. 57. Ethinylestradiol increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lomitapide doses should not exceed 30 mg/day. Use caution and monitor therapy. 58. Ethinylestradiol reduces the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs. Higher growth hormone doses may be required. Use caution and monitor therapy. 59. Drospirenone reduces the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs. Higher growth hormone doses may be required. Use caution and monitor therapy. 60. Lorlatinib reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 61. Drospirenone and lornoxicam both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 62. Losartan and drospirenone both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 63. Lumefantrine reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 64. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Initiation of weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may require a reduced mavacamten dose. Use caution and monitor therapy. 65. Drospirenone and meclofenamate both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 66. Drospirenone and mefenamic acid both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 67. Drospirenone and meloxicam both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 68. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while metaproterenol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 69. Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drospirenone also reduces the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 70. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while methyclothiazide decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 71. Metronidazole may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 72. Drospirenone increases serum potassium, while metolazone decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor therapy closely. 73. Metoprolol and drospirenone both increase serum potassium. Therapy should be modified, and potassium levels monitored closely. 74. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 75. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. This may prolong sedation. Use caution and monitor therapy. 76. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with mild CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to midazolam, prolonging sedation. Use caution and monitor therapy. 77. Mifepristone reduces the effects of ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Backup contraceptive methods are recommended. 78. Mifepristone reduces the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Backup contraceptive methods are recommended. 79. Minocycline may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 80. Moexipril and drospirenone may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia due to pharmacodynamic interactions. Use caution and monitor potassium levels.
